prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: I need to add an infant in arms to a reservation for tomorrow morning but it's a two hour wait on the reservations line.  Is this something I can do at the airport tomorrow?
Delta: Hi Jay, can you DM your confirmation # to the link provided? I will be glad to help. *TBT https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: can I get assistance adding infant in arms to an existing reservation? Not being given callback option via phone and wait is 2+ hrs.
Delta: 2/2 https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: . Not trying to whine or complain but we’ve been awake for 30 hours, traveling for 12, with a 10 month old baby. Now, 2 hours from home we are told we need a separate ticket for our infant in arms (who is listed on b. pass)... supposedly a new rule? No trouble 2 hrs ago.
Delta: Hi. Please DM your confirmation code, so I may be of assistance. Thanks. *TMA

Customer: on flight 5254 ATL to HPN. Toilet smell is overwhelming. I have an infant who doesn't need to breathe this shit (literally)
Delta: ...issues have already been reported. Thanks for your feedback, Anna. *AMV 2/2

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: general_question):
"""Is there anything I need to do if I am traveling with an infant in arms?"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Hi! Please DM us your reservation info so we can help you with traveling with an infant in arms. https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m
